# Retrospective: PR 12776

## Worked

Fresh native Opus 5.5 High and Sol Xhigh sessions, equivalent neutral scope, pre-launch bounded security triage, no peer-report reads before independent finals, source-first stopping criteria. Sol appropriately stopped at source scope. Opus's extracted QtQuick subtree established a useful baseline/head contrast without touching the live desktop. Coordinator checked raw results and controls, not only the seal or summary. The public draft remains scoped and contains no generic test filler.

## Friction and deviations

See REPORT.md and reviewers/fable/audit-addendum.md for full retained evidence. Early coordinator fetch receipts were incomplete; later fetches split stdout, stderr and exit. Opus used host file availability checks and name-resolving listings, exceeded the 60-line policy-read bound once, and wrote process memories outside the assignment. These violated explicit process constraints; private history is preserved and not laundered into a compliance claim. No host runtime/desktop action or account experiment followed.

Qt logging did not reach captured stderr in v1. A failed edit was batched with pin/run in v2, which therefore repeated v1. Both invalid runs are retained and excluded. v3 forced stderr logging and applied edit/hash/pin/run sequentially. The report's “full range” wording was clarified as configured endpoints plus initial motion, not a measured traversal or loop.

## Corrections

PROCESS-CORRECTIONS.md records the explicit assignment correction sent to the owned reviewer: no outside-root intentional memory writes, numeric metadata only, dependency checks inside review.py, <=60-line policy reads, sequential edit/hash/pin/run, separate fetch streams/status, precise motion-window wording. Native history and invalid artifacts must remain intact. Process lessons belong in this retrospective, not an unassigned CLI memory directory.

No confirmed Omadev or review.py bug. No desktop capacity needed. Native Qt logging routing is a fixture concern, not a PR failure. Preserve the distinction between synthetic Qt behavior and the full target desktop in future assignments; do not carry this PR's conclusions into a new session.
comment:
**Verified:** No actionable defect found in the scoped review of `31f910df`. The media marquee change restarts with settled geometry and resets the label when scrolling stops.

A synthetic QtQuick comparison used the extracted [`scrollClip` block](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/31f910dff8fa1f0ab00aaa5de606ed119ac256e0/shell/plugins/services/media/BarWidget.qml#L47-L94), with synthetic surrounding objects and a fixed font size:

| Transition | Baseline | PR head |
|---|---|---|
| Empty → long title | Stayed at `x=0` despite `running=true` | Position advanced with settled animation endpoints |
| Long → short title | Retained a nonzero offset | Stopped at `x=0` |
| Popup opens / bar becomes vertical | Retained the scrolling offset | Stopped at `x=0`; scrolling restarted when eligible again |

Source inspection also confirms that text and implicit-width changes schedule a restart even when scrolling remains eligible, avoiding reuse of the previous title’s animation geometry.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Qt 6.11.2, offscreen software rendering, extracted-code comparison against merge-base `8f324c90`. Motion was sampled for up to 1.5 seconds per state, not a complete traversal or loop. No live Quickshell/MPRIS, lock/unlock, CPU/battery testing, or full shell test suite. This does not establish target-desktop visual behavior or performance.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection; independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments; Astra synthesis checked claims against source and the recorded Qt comparison. Sol’s assessment was source-only.
